articleTitle: Analysing of diverse stress pattern in ECG using machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: ECG signals are commonly used to diagnose various cardiac conditions, and the classification of these signals is an important task in Stress identification. With the advancement of ML techniques, several ML models have been developed to classify ECG signals with high accuracy. This paper aims to review recent studies that use ML models for ECG classification, equivalence to the working nature of different prototype, and discuss the challenges and limitations of these models. The study found that deep learning models, such as CNNs and RNNs, outperformed traditional ML models in terms of closeness and validity. The results also showed that the combination of multiple models could improve the classification performance. However, the study also highlighted the need for large annotated ECG datasets and the requirement of domain expertise for feature engineering. Overall, this review provides a complete analysis of the current state of ECG classification using ML models and identifies areas for future research and improvement. Even though the accuracy of ML models in ECG classification is not always perfect, they can still provide valuable information and support to healthcare professionals. In some cases, even a lower accuracy can still be useful, especially in the context of large-scale screening and monitoring programs, where the goal is to identify individuals who require further evaluation. In these cases, the high computational speed and scalability of ML models make them an attractive option, as they can quickly process large amounts of data and provide preliminary results that can be followed up with more comprehensive and accurate tests. Additionally, the results from ML models can also be used as a starting point for further analysis by healthcare professionals, who can use their domain knowledge to interpret the results and make informed decisions. Therefore, despite their limitations, ML models can still play an vital role in the field of Electrocardiogram classification and contribute to improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Feature based cognitive analysis in sports and non-sports individuals using real-time EEG
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) plays a vital role to analyse the cognitive ability. The present study investigates cognitive performance in both resting and active states among sports and non-sports individuals through real-time EEG signals collected from frontal and parietal electrodes (F3, F4, P3, and P4). A rigorous preprocessing pipeline, including filtering technique and Independent Component Analysis (ICA), was utilized to enhance data quality by reducing noise and artifacts. Both linear and non-linear features were extracted, and feature selection was performed using Mutual Information (MuI) to pinpoint the most relevant attributes for cognitive assessment. The selected features were fed into using five machine learning classifiers namely viz Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF). The results indicates that SVM achieved a classification accuracy of 93%, surpassing the other classifiers in differentiating cognitive ability between sports and non-sports individuals.

articleTitle: Multi-class classification and pretrained sustainable agriculture model for plant leaf disease detection using ResNet-101
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In recent years, advancements in technology have greatly benefited the agricultural sector. One critical aspect of ensuring healthy plant growth is promptly identifying infected leaves. For sustainable agriculture, automatically detecting diseased on plant leaves before the infection spreads is highly advantageous. This paper introduces deep learning models like CNN, along with various optimization techniques and hyperparameter tuning being used. The study utilizes machine learning frameworks and a deep learning library. It encompasses 10 different datasets comprising 151,007 leaf images depicting 270 different diseases, including healthy leaves from 44 plant species. Additionally, pretrained models such as AlexNet, ResNet50, GoogLeNet, DenseNet-121, and ResNet101 are employed, with the ResNet model achieving the highest accuracy rate of 94.45%.

articleTitle: A systematic review on the application of IoT in agriculture
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Agriculture contributes to 18% of the economy of India. The authors have found that the Internet of Things (IoT) has been crucial in empowering agriculture. It has helped farmers in varied ways, such as providing information about weather conditions, soil quality standards, temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind speed and its direction, etc. From many surveys it has proved that IoT contributes 20% to Crop monitoring, 17% to Farm management, and 14% to disease detection. Thus, IoT has made farming more efficient and easier. It has also enabled the farmers to pre-plan the next season's crops and their prerequisites. IoT also enhances crop production and reduces crop mortality rates. IoT utilization for precision agriculture can increase the yield by 10-20% by optimizing planting, watering, and fertilization. On the other hand, implementing an IoT-enabled irrigation system can improve water usage efficiency resulting in a net yield increase of 20-30%, while monitoring crop health and soil conditions can lead to an increase in productivity by 10-15%. IoT sensors and data analytics can help in the early detection of pests and diseases reducing crop loss by 30-35%. IoT-based applications are very important for farming and they make farming smarter.

articleTitle: AquaVision Dehaze and enhancement: a robust algorithm for improving underwater image quality in aquatic environments
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Underwater imaging is frequently challenged by light scattering, leading to haze, color distortion, and visibility loss. To address these issues, we introduce the AquaVision Dehaze and Enhancement algorithm to improve underwater image quality. Extensive testing on a dataset from an aquaculture environment demonstrates that the algorithm significantly enhances image clarity. Quantitative evaluations reveal high performance across various image quality metrics, with scores of UICM (19.6463), UISM (18.1490), UIConM (26.7463), and UIQM (13.3312). Furthermore, the algorithm delivers competitive results in no-reference image quality metrics, including NIQE (3.6780), Entropy (7.5942), PIQE (52.1444), and BRISQUE (35.9847). These results highlight the algorithm’s effectiveness in addressing the challenges of underwater imaging and illustrate the effectiveness through an ablation study. The AquaVision Dehaze and Enhancement algorithm offers a robust solution for improving the quality making it a valuable tool for advancing research in aquatic environments.

articleTitle: Identification of tomato diseases effectively using an attention-based EfficientNet model
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual data. Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs), specifically designed to classify images, have revolutionized the field of computer vision. In spite of their success, these models often struggle to precisely localize critical regions of interest and encounter difficulties in distinguishing between images with highly similar characteristics, leading to classification errors. Agriculture plays a pivotal role in global sustainability. Therefore, accurate identification of plant diseases is crucial to mitigate substantial economic losses. Tomato is an economically important crop, and tomato diseases often exhibit symptoms that could be confusingly similar, making accurate diagnosis challenging. To address localization and similarity issues in tomato diseases, this study proposes a multi-head attention-based EfficientNetB0 model. The proposed model was trained and tested on field-condition images of tomato diseases. The tomato dataset consists of nine tomato diseases, including healthy images, and has a total of 8789 images. The proposed model achieved 97.4% test accuracy, which is a slight improvement compared to the baseline EfficientNetB0 model. Also, the proposed model exhibited the lowest rate of misclassifications. Furthermore, the Score-CAM technique was employed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, and explanations generated by the Score-CAM demonstrated the significant performance of the model in localizing disease symptoms.

articleTitle: Advanced Glaucoma detection using CNN models integrated with random forest classifier for enhanced diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Glaucoma is a prevalent retinal disease worldwide, leading to irreversible blindness if not diagnosed early. This research aims to distinguish glaucomatous eyes from normal eyes using an innovative glaucoma detection framework that integrates a Random Forest classifier with VGG-19 and ResNet50 models. The proposed method aggregates classification outcomes from Random Forest, VGG-19, and ResNet50 models through a post-processing decision block to deliver the final classification. This approach addresses limitations of existing techniques, significantly enhancing diagnostic accuracy and robustness by leveraging the strengths of these models. The framework, developed through ensemble modeling, achieves an accuracy of 96.10%, a precision rate of 99.10%, a recall rate of 89.00%, and an F1-score of 94.20%. Our research underscores the importance of integrating conventional optic disc measurement methods with image shape-derived features in machine learning models, enabling early and precise glaucoma diagnosis.

articleTitle: Agrisense: MyRio and LabVIEW-powered precision farming for sustainable agriculture
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Agrisense is a precision farming solution using MyRio hardware and LabVIEW software to advance sustainable agriculture. By integrating sensors for soil moisture, climate monitoring, and crop health, it continuously collects real-time data. LabVIEW processes this data through advanced algorithms, supporting data-driven decision-making in agriculture. Agrisense optimizes resource allocation, such as water, fertilizers, and pesticides, enhancing crop yield and resource efficiency. With remote monitoring capabilities, users can access real-time data and manage operations from anywhere. Agrisense not only transforms traditional farming but also fosters sustainability by minimizing resource waste, making it a pivotal tool in addressing global food security.

articleTitle: Emotion detection in children with autism spectrum disorder: leveraging EEG signals and companion bots for enhanced interaction
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often struggle with emotional recognition and expression, which can hinder their social interactions and communication skills. Detecting emotions in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder is crucial for understanding their emotional states, as these children often face challenges in recognizing and expressing feelings. This paper explores the facial emotions and EEG signals for emotion detection with machine learning, deep learning, and physiological signal. The results show substantial accuracy in recognizing emotions by utilizing multimodal data and powerful algorithms, providing insightful information for educators and caregivers. Our goal in modifying YOLO for emotion identification is to take use of its accuracy and speed in dynamic contexts like real-time video streams. The study assesses how effectively the YOLO architectures—more especially, YOLOv5s, YOLOv7-tiny, and YOLOv8s—perform on a customized dataset intended for the identification of emotions in kids with ASD. The results demonstrate the models' efficacy in precisely recognizing emotional expressions, which supports therapeutic interventions for kids with ASD.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT security: a trust-centric random forest approach for blackhole node detection
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The Proposed Model enhances node classification and security in IoT networks by incorporating a Random Forest algorithm to classify nodes as either blackhole or non-blackhole nodes. The Proposed Model utilizes a diverse range of metrics including Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), Packet Loss, Throughput, Jitter, Latency, Reliability, and Energy Consumption. These metrics are used to train the Random Forest classifier, allowing for accurate identification of malicious nodes attempting blackhole attacks. The Random Forest algorithm, a powerful ensemble learning technique, creates multiple decision trees based on the trust metrics, each making an independent classification. The final classification is determined by majority voting across all the trees. This process improves the detection accuracy by taking into account multiple metrics rather than relying on a single parameter. The combination of this algorithm with the comprehensive trust metrics allows the Proposed Model to better differentiate between benign and malicious nodes, ensuring that only trustworthy nodes are chosen for routing. Simulations were performed to evaluate the performance of the Proposed Model in comparison to RPL and the trust-based approach by Mustafa Ghaleb et al. (2021). The simulations demonstrated that the Random Forest-enhanced model achieved a higher detection accuracy of blackhole nodes, resulting in improved Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) and throughput. Additionally, the Proposed Model exhibited lower average delay compared to the traditional approaches. By leveraging the Random Forest algorithm, the Proposed Model can more effectively detect and isolate suspicious nodes, preventing them from disrupting network operations. This ensures that the network is both secure and efficient, making it particularly suited for critical IoT applications such as military and battlefield scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced biometrics face morph detection via neural style transfer and 2D wavelet transformation
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Biometric feature identification has grown in popularity during the past a decade. Nowadays, many mobile devices are fitted with common components such as fingerprint sensors and high-quality video, which have grown more affordable. Even systems requiring strict security regulations, such as border control at airports, have turned to biometric technologies due to their advanced precision in facial recognition. This study proposes an approach to detection based on 2D Wavelet Transformation and Progressive Enhanced Learning Framework (PELF). Additionally, using the neural morph enhancement process, to study Deep Learning-based Neural Style Transfer (Deep-NST) model was developed to identify morphing face images with features resembling those of the input images. To precisely capture the features and texture changes in the image, our approach first extracts high-frequency information from all three color channels. Next, a progressive enhanced learning framework was built to combine high-frequency data with RGB information. Furthermore, the framework that is suggested for assessing the quality of our method and contrasting it with existing DNN interpretability techniques. Deep-NST is superior to other methods in identifying abnormalities. When the DNN provides an incorrect or confused evaluation, this becomes extremely crucial.

articleTitle: Plastic image detection from UAV images using YOLOV8
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental issue that demands innovative monitoring solutions. This study utilizes the YOLOv8 deep learning algorithm in combination with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with high-resolution cameras to automate plastic detection in aerial imagery. A custom drone dataset, with 85% of the images containing plastic, was developed to evaluate detection performance. The results demonstrate that YOLOv8 can effectively identify plastic in complex environments, offering a scalable and efficient alternative to traditional ground surveys. However, challenges such as varied plastic types, sizes, and visual complexity remain. This UAV-based approach shows promise for large-scale applications, including tracking cleanup initiatives, mapping plastic distribution, and assessing environmental impacts. Future research could improve this methodology by incorporating advanced image processing techniques to address plastic variability and enhance detection accuracy. Overall, the findings highlight UAVs as a valuable tool for comprehensive plastic pollution monitoring and contribute to advancing environmental conservation efforts.

articleTitle: Various approaches of spectrogram for CNN-based classification of Parkinson's and healthy speech
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder on a global scale. The present method for identifying Parkinson's disease is costly and time-consuming. In recent times, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), a deep learning technique have gained ground in automatic classification because of their potential to extract complex nonlinear patterns from input data. This work compares the accuracy of the CNN model for the spectrogram in DB and non-DB scales and divides the obtained spectrograms into low-frequency and high-frequency spectrograms in both scales. This is achievable because the convolution layer in CNN automatically gains knowledge of the relevant features from the spectrograms. In this work, our model achieves a competitive classification accuracy of 100% using a low-frequency spectrogram in a non-DB scale which is half the frequency component of the actual spectrogram which demonstrates the effectiveness of the low-frequency component of the spectrogram in distinguishing Parkinson's speech and healthy controls. This study spotlights the capacity of deep learning in creating non-intrusive, automated algorithms for the early identification and investigation of Parkinson's disease, therefore facilitating the development of more easily accessible and precise diagnostic instruments.

articleTitle: Smart traffic management: a deep learning revolution in traffic prediction - a review
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In the era of smart cities and autonomous vehicles, efficient traffic management is critical to reducing congestion, enhancing safety, and improving overall urban mobility. Traditional traffic prediction models, while effective to a certain extent, often fall short in handling the complexities of modern traffic patterns influenced by a multitude of factors such as weather, events, and fluctuating demand. This paper presents a novel approach to traffic prediction leveraging the power of deep learning. Deep Learning, a subset of machine learning, excels in identifying intricate patterns within large datasets. By employing advanced neural network architectures such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), captures both temporal and spatial dependencies in traffic data. The model is trained on extensive historical traffic datasets, integrating additional contextual information such as meteorological data and public event schedules to enhance predictive accuracy. Deep learning models demonstrate traditional statistical methods like ARIMA in forecasting traffic volume and congestion levels. The results reveal an improvement in prediction accuracy, particularly sudden traffic surges and mitigating the impact of unforeseen disruptions. The potential of deep learning revolutionizes traffic prediction, paving smarter, more responsive urban traffic control.

articleTitle: A survey of machine learning applications in medical imaging for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of brain degenerative disorders particularly Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, have incurred a dire need for effective diagnostic methodologies. With advancements in medical imaging techniques and Artificial Intelligence (AI), transformative potential exists to enhance early detection and disease classification. This review examines the recent progress made in the use of diagnostic medical imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Despite significant progress, a comprehensive overview is lacking. The review aims to summarize and synthesize existing methods, critically evaluate their strengths and limitations, and identify emerging trends. Multimodal imaging data, combining information from different sources like MRI, PET, and SPECT, has shown progress in improving diagnostic accuracy and providing insights into disease progression. Advanced AI techniques, such as transfer learning and generative adversarial networks, have further enhanced the performance of diagnostic models. Previous studies have predominantly focused on using standalone techniques, often leaving the integration of multi-modal imaging and deep learning methodologies that could lead to more robust diagnostic frameworks. This literature review addresses this gap by synthesizing current research on medical imaging modalities, AI applications, and their implications in diagnosing Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. This review seeks to connect technological innovations with clinical applications to establish more robust and dependable diagnostic methods.

articleTitle: A comprehensive analysis on diverse algorithms used for sentiment analysis and classification of twitter data
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Twitter is a social platform that allows millions of people across the world share their thoughts and ideas, bringing out new connections with large number of audiences. So, whether it’s an event or any latest news people share their views on that with others publicly through this platform. Twitter is being used widely for reporting, marketing, PR Teams, individuals et cetera . Twitter data sentiment analysis has been popular in the research field within the past few years as it helps in getting idea about people’s opinion, their likes and dislikes about certain things, market insights, environmental impact and analysis of customers for m arket product. In this paper a detailed systematic review has been recited about all the past research carried in the field of twit ter data sentiment analysis, various techniques that were used in the process of twitter data mining are analyzed, also the areas where twitters data sentiment analysis has been implemented across many years are being presented along with various challenges that could b e encountered in the future with possible scope of research. This paper is divided into different sections starting with the wo rkflow of twitter data analysis process, section second categorized all the approaches used for twitter data sentiment analysis, third section summarized all the algorithms developed in the past followed by the last section where common findings and gaps are presented .

articleTitle: Prospective applications of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance consistent attention in first-year undergraduate students in the education sector
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Attention is a critical factor in effective learning, particularly for first-year undergraduate students adapting to the demands of higher education. However, maintaining consistent focus poses a challenge, often exacerbated by increased digital distractions and cognitive overload. Education could be revolutionized by artificial intelligence (AI) by becoming more individualized, effective, and accessible. AI has the potential to significantly enhance teaching and learning in the educational system through a variety of tools and applications, such as Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS), Chatbots, Virtual Assistants, Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and Personalized Learning Platforms. This study explores the prospective applications of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance and sustain attention among first-year undergraduates in the educational sector. The study aims to identify specific AI solutions that monitor engagement, provide real-time feedback, and adapt content based on individual attention needs, ultimately improving students' academic performance and overall learning experience. Through a quantitative methods approach involving surveys, user testing, and data analysis, this research seeks to provide insights into the effectiveness of AI tools in fostering student focus. Findings from this study will contribute to the growing body of knowledge on AI's role in education, offering practical recommendations for institutions looking to integrate AI-based solutions to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes, particularly at the critical first-year level.

articleTitle: Pose-critical keypoint attention model for dynamic yoga pose classification
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Yoga pose detection and classification have garnered considerable attention in recent years due to their significant applications in various domains, including fitness, health monitoring, and rehabilitation programs. Accurate detection and classification of yoga poses not only enhance the effectiveness of fitness regimes but also facilitate the assessment of practitioners’ health and recovery processes. However, existing methods often struggle with the challenges posed by high-dimensional data processing, particularly in real-time applications. This paper introduces the Pose-Critical Keypoint Attention (PCKA) model, a novel approach designed to overcome the limitations of traditional methods in yoga pose analysis. The PCKA model employs an advanced attention mechanism to dynamically prioritize the most relevant keypoints from a comprehensive set of 33 extracted keypoints. This dynamic focus allows for efficient classification without the drawbacks associated with static keypoint reduction, ensuring that the model remains adaptable and robust across various poses. Extensive experiments evaluate the performance of the PCKA model against conventional classification frameworks. The results indicate that this model significantly outperforms traditional approaches, achieving an impressive accuracy of 91.08%, precision of 89.70%, recall of 91.93%, and an F1-score of 90.78%. These metrics demonstrate the model’s capability to deliver accurate pose classification while providing real-time feedback for corrective measures, which is crucial for users striving to improve their yoga practices.

articleTitle: Knee osteoarthritis detection an AI driven severity estimation
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In this work, we use the Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grading system to investigate deep learning models or the automated detection and classification of knee osteoarthritis (OA) from radiographs. For prompt care, early identification of knee arthritis is essential, and radiography is an affordable, widely available diagnostic method. We evaluated the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of a number of cutting-edge models, including VGG16, Xception, DenseNet121, InceptionV3, ResNet50, and EfficientNet07. With testing accuracy of 96.90% and 95.90%, respectively, and strong F1 scores of 0.9690 and 0.9790, Xception and InceptionV3 outperformed the other models under evaluation, demonstrating robust performance and trustworthy generalization. While ResNet50, EfficientNet07, and an ensemble model had lower accuracy and F1 scores, indicating possible limitations, DenseNet121 and VGG16 also shown strong performance in dealing with the complex knee arthritis grading system. According to our research, Xception and InceptionV3 are very good at automatically classifying knee OA, providing potential instruments for clinical treatment planning and early identification.

articleTitle: Turmeric leaf disease detection using optimized deep learning model
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Turmeric is popular for its medicinal, culinary, and non-culinary uses. Turmeric cultivation is affected due to disease in their leaves. Farmers conventionally identify the leaf diseases and provide pesticides to avoid further loss. However, manual identification of leaf disease over large farms is time-consuming and requires human effort. Also, in several types of leaf disease, the specific type that occurs in the plant should be distinguished; thus, proper knowledge of farming is required. To simplify this and to know the type of disease, smart agricultural practices are followed worldwide. One of the intelligent techniques adopted in farming is leaf disease detection. By providing the filed image to a learning algorithm, the type of disease can be detected accurately without manual interventions. ML and DL are used in this smart agricultural practice. To improve the performance further, an optimized deep learning model is presented in this research work. A Novel gazelle optimization algorithm is combined with deep learning MobileNetV3 network to attain enhanced disease detection performance. Experimentation on our own dataset with 5000 samples, including leaf spot, leaf blight, leaf rot, and curl disease-affected leaves, the proposed model performance is evaluated and observed with a maximum accuracy of 96.8%, a precision of 97.1% over conventional disease detection models.

articleTitle: Object detection in haze for UAV using DCP and YOLO
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The phenomenon of haze poses a significant challenge in UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) surveillance, particularly under the computational constraints inherent to UAV systems. This paper proposes a sophisticated yet efficient approach to overcome these limitations by integrating algorithms like dark channel prior (DCP), dynamic gamma correction, bilateral filtering, and YOLOv8 object detection. The DCP algorithm effectively clears haze from images by manipulating pixel intensity values, this process is further optimized using bilateral filtering for computational efficiency. These dehazed images are put thorough dynamic gamma correction which further enhances image clarity by dynamically adjusting gamma values for each image. The YOLOv8 architecture, selected for its low computational footprint and superior accuracy, performs object detection and localization on processed images. Using the CVPR 2024 Haze Detection Challenge dataset, the proposed model demonstrates superior performance, achieving a high confidence score and a detection accuracy of 92%, exceeding the capabilities of existing models. These results underscore the method’s effectiveness in addressing haze-related challenges within the computational limits of UAVs.

articleTitle: GMM based deep convolutional neural network for Leukemia diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Leukaemia, a complex and heterogeneous group of blood cancer raises significant challenges in diagnosis due to its diverse subtypes and molecular characteristics. Recent advancements in genomic and molecular technologies have opened new avenues for improving diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment strategies. This paper explores the journey towards enhancing the accuracy of Leukemia diagnosis, highlighting key innovations in genomic profiling, machine learning algorithms, and biomarker identification. By integrating these cutting-edge approaches, the paper demonstrates how precision medicine can revolutionize Leukaemia care, leading to better patient outcomes and a deeper understanding of the disease's underlying mechanisms. The findings underscore the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous research in the quest to combat Leukaemia more effectively.

articleTitle: Enhanced sales analysis: predictive insights from machine learning models using the XGboost regressor approach
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In the contemporary retail landscape, major department stores and Big Marts meticulously track individual product sales data to anticipate future consumer demand and optimize inventory management. These extensive data repositories encompass a wealth of customer information and specific product attributes housed in a centralized data warehouse. By mining this data store, anomalies and overarching patterns are identified, forming the basis for predicting future sales volumes through advanced machine learning techniques tailored for retail establishments such as Big Mart. This paper introduces a predictive model utilizing the XGBoost Regressor approach to forecast sales for a company like Big Mart, demonstrating enhanced performance compared to existing models.

articleTitle: Evaluation of RPL and SDN-WISE in UAV assisted WSN data collection
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of the Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL) and the Software-Defined WIreless SEnsor network (SDN-WISE) approach in a IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Net-works (6LoWPAN) network scenario. In this network scenario a mobile sink acting as an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is used for data collection in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). A novel methodology is presented for generating efficient paths for the mobile UAV sink. It involves leveraging the K means clustering algorithm for finding the centroids which can cover the sensors within the transmission range. The Ant Colony Optimization technique is then used for traversing the centroids to solve the Travelling Salesmen problem (TSP). Key performance metrics such as average end-to-end delay, packet delivery ratio and energy consumption are analysed under varying conditions and sensor node densities. The study provides valuable insights into optimising UAV-assisted WSNs for enhanced performance and longevity in real-world applications.

articleTitle: SE-VGGNet: Liver tumor detection using squeeze excited VGG network
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Liver tumors, including metastatic cancer and cholangiocarcinoma, pose a significant threat to global health, necessitating accurate and timely detection. This paper presents a novel deep learning model, SE-VGGNet, for liver tumor classification, which innovatively combines Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks with a VGGNet backbone. This integration enhances feature extraction by allowing the model to recalibrate channel-wise feature responses, focusing more effectively on the most relevant image regions. SE-VGGNet was evaluated on a liver tumor dataset, achieving a classification accuracy of 99.09%, precision of 98.15%, and recall of 100%, significantly outperforming traditional CNN and VGG-16 models. The novelty of this approach lies in its ability to achieve high performance even with small datasets, addressing a critical challenge in medical imaging. Additionally, this method offers the potential for broader application to other medical imaging tasks, highlighting its adaptability and impact on early cancer diagnosis and clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Lane detection and traffic sign detection for autonomous driving systems
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In the realm of autonomous driving, this study focuses on two critical tasks for scene understanding: lane detection and traffic sign detection. These tasks are essential to ensuring safe and reliable navigation in self-driving systems. A combination of traditional computer vision techniques and modern deep learning methods are used to achieve accurate detection and analysis of lanes and traffic signs in real-world driving scenarios. For lane detection, we utilize edge detection and the Hough Transform, while for traffic sign detection, we apply machine learning algorithms to recognize and classify various signs. This hybrid approach demonstrates the potential of integrating classical computer vision algorithms with deep learning models to enhance the perception capabilities of autonomous vehicles. The model achieves a balanced performance, with accuracy metrics ranging from 80-90% across both tasks, indicating a robust ability to detect lanes and signs effectively under varied conditions. This work serves as a foundation for developing more advanced scene understanding systems in autonomous driving technology. In the future, we aim to enhance the model’s adaptability through continuous learning and incorporating additional sensory data, such as LiDAR and radar. Additionally, expanding the dataset and testing the models in diverse environmental conditions, including different lighting and weather scenarios, will further improve the robustness and reliability.

articleTitle: Machine learning strategies for human stress level prediction: a comparative performance analysis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: This review paper offers a thorough examination of current machine learning models for estimating human stress levels, with particular attention to Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. A rigorous analysis of these models' performance, benefits, and drawbacks highlights their potential for prediction and stress management. The review examines how each model's architecture and features impact the predictability, accuracy, and interpretability of results. It identifies future objectives and research gaps, including the integration of multimodal data, emotion recognition, and explainable AI systems. This review aims to inform researchers and professionals involved in stress prediction and management to help develop more effective stress management solutions.

articleTitle: An overview of personal data protection in mobile IoT based upon a bibliometric analysis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) fosters innovation and connectivity but also heightens personal data vulnerability, raising concerns data privacy and integrity. Although adaptive security mechanisms have been introduced, their effectiveness remains uncertain, calling for ongoing research. This paper provides a bibliometric analysis and a review of current methods for personal data protection in mobile IoT systems. Based on Scopus database data, 390 publications from 264 sources were identified, authored by 1,238 researchers between 2010 and 2023, through four primary languages. The analysis indicates 32.55% annual increase in scientific output, with an average of 3.53 co-authors per document and an international collaboration rate of 24.36%. Results showed that data protection in mobile IoT relies on strengthening IoT infrastructures and regulatory compliance, integrating cryptographic algorithms and blockchain for confidentiality and non-repudiation. The Covid-19 pandemic has heightened the focus on IoT data security, underscoring the field's increasing significance.

articleTitle: An anonymity communication method for IoT based electronic health record
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: With the exponential growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) in the healthcare sector, safeguarding sensitive data has become paramount. In healthcare services system, health and medical data that contains privacy information are often transmitted among networks, and such privacy information should be protected. Therefore, there is a need for privacy preserving data collection scheme to protect clients (patients) data. This study delves into the protection of IoT data from wearable device through a combination of P-sensitivity and K-anonymization techniques. We examine how these techniques can enhance privacy and security in healthcare applications. By employing P-sensitivity to limit the disclosure risk of individual data points and K-anonymization to anonymize datasets, we create a robust framework for data protection. This study contributes to the ongoing efforts to secure IoT data in healthcare, ensuring the responsible and confidential use of patient information.

articleTitle: A dynamic cloud index data searching using random forest algorithm
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Given the fact that cloud computing is prevalent in modern organizations, proper dynamic indexing plays a critical role of supporting an efficient method of storing and retrieving such information. The purpose of this research is to apply the random forest algorithms in improving the means of indexing and searching the data stored in the cloud storage systems. The scheme called dynamic cloud indexing system takes benefits of random forest algorithm because of its flexibility in dealing with the multiple data types and their interconnection. Due to the limitations of indexing in traditional methods used in applications, the system is adaptive to the structural changes and cloud deployment formation. The prototype augments the function of indexing by utilizing random forest algorithms that enhance the retrieval of data. Live retraining capability implies that the index model constantly used to analyze the data allows it to update its training from time to time. Sandbox experiments on various datasets mimic actual implementation paradigms, whereby the proposed system’s efficiency is measured based on scalability, accuracy, and search speed. Thus, the findings of the study reveal the capacity of action in improving the efficiency and flexibility of random forest algorithms within cloud data management, thus establishing the framework for complex cloud data indexing procedures.

articleTitle: Smart fire extinguishing drone: integration of Raspberry Pi and multi-sensor systems
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: In the context of increasing fire accidents and the significant risks faced by first responders, there is a pressing need for innovative solutions to mitigate these dangers. This paper presents the development of a fire extinguishing drone system leveraging Raspberry Pi technology. The system aims to enhance firefighting operations by deploying drones equipped with sensors capable of locating fire origins both manually and automatically. Through the utilization of Raspberry Pi, the drones demonstrate exceptional mobility and agility, reducing risks to human life during firefighting missions. Furthermore, the system facilitates rapid data transmission, enabling firefighters to access crucial information promptly. The proposed solution holds promise in improving the efficiency and safety of firefighting operations, thereby addressing the challenges associated with traditional firefighting methods.

articleTitle: Integrating NAO V6 robot for enhanced face recognition in security system
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: NAO robot is a humanoid robot designed to help human assisted task with the interaction of humans. It will be used for many applications including teaching, help desk for banking sectors, facial recognition and many human related tasks. The proposed methodology deals a facial recognition technique with a set of information’s collected from different people. Choregraphe software tool is used for integrating NAO robot for face recognition applications. The developed modules can recognize different faces and give the respective response through programming. Though the conventional face recognition method takes more time to recognize human faces. Implementation of Convolution Neural Network (CNN) algorithm improves accuracy which also provides instant recognition & response from the NAO robot. The results prove that the implementation is a cost effective and highly efficient method to improve face recognition. This proposed methodology intended to develop a module capable of accurately identifying and authenticating individuals through facial biometrics with the use of CNN for efficient and reliable process. By utilizing Choregraphe's software tool and the advanced capabilities of NAO robots, the proposed system offers a seamless and user-friendly authentication process.

articleTitle: Towards smart and sustainable cities: integrating ARIMA-ARNN and IoT for public lighting management - a Romanian town case study
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The efficient management of public lighting systems is essential for reducing energy consumption and costs in small towns. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting model that combines the strengths of the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average and Artificial Neural Network techniques to predict the energy consumption of public lighting in a small town in Romania for 12 months. Leveraging data on the energy usage of the town's public lighting system, the study uses the ARIMA-ARNN hybrid model to provide accurate and reliable forecasts that can assist town managers in budgeting for their energy needs and planning for IoT-enabled smart lighting systems implementation. The findings demonstrate that the hybrid model outperforms traditional individual models in terms of predictive accuracy, making it a valuable tool for energy consumption forecasting and management in the public lighting sector.

articleTitle: Early prediction of Alzheimer’s disease using magnetic resonance images (MRI) in leveraging deep learning models
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a well-known illness characterized by memory loss and cognitive decline. Since current treatments work best in the early stages, early detection is vital for effective management. The Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) plays a key role in diagnosing Alzheimer's by providing detailed images of brain structures. Advances in deep learning have further improved MRI-based diagnosis through automated image analysis.EfficientNetB2 and MobileNetV3 are lightweight convolutional neural networks (CNNs) known for their high performance and speed, making them ideal for resource-limited and real-time applications.InceptionV3 is a widely used CNN, known for its strong performance in image classification tasks. By training these deep learning models on complete MRI datasets, they offer the potential to aid doctors in making accurate and timely diagnoses. This approach couldlead to better outcomes and improved quality of life for patients.The research aims to enhance early detection and treatment methods for Alzheimer's disease, contributing to advancements in deep learning models.

articleTitle: Improved border protection: An innovative approach to detect face morphing attacks
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Facial morphing attacks have shown to be a serious risk to the passport issue process, undermining border security measures. It is quite difficult to identify an attack on a morphing facial image that has been printed, scanned, and re-digitized in order to obtain a passport. This research explores a detection method that minimizes the blending-induced deterioration of images. Focused Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (FLRP) is the important part of this approach. A neural network with deep learning may be trained to identify between a real and a morphed facial image by using specific parts of the image, which this framework describes to a human inspection at the pixel level. Analysis and results from experiments indicate that this technique may significantly improve the accuracy of facial morphing attack detection. This method exhibits significant robustness and high computational efficiency when compared to the current approaches. It offers a lot of possible applications for improving the facial recognition system's security.

articleTitle: Detection of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks with crow search optimization algorithm and artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach to detect Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks using the Crow Search Optimization Algorithm (CSOA) for feature dimensionality reduction combined with Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classification. CSOA effectively reduces feature redundancy, optimizing relevant features for improved accuracy. After feature reduction, ANN is trained on the optimized set to classify normal and attack traffic. Various optimization algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), were evaluated for comparison. GA achieved an accuracy of 96.10%, while ACO and PSO performed slightly better, reaching 97.08% and 97.01% respectively. The proposed CSOA-ANN method outperformed all other algorithms with an accuracy of 98.50%, precision of 98.94%, recall of 98.04%, and F1 score of 98.49%. This approach not only demonstrates high accuracy but also offers an efficient and energy-saving solution, making it an optimal choice for network security in DDoS detection. The CSOA-ANN model’s effectiveness in enhancing classification accuracy underscores its potential for robust intrusion detection in cybersecurity applications.

articleTitle: Real-time crop analysis with enhanced image classification using deep learning and fuzzy logic techniques
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The proposed research presents a smart irrigation system is designed to optimize agricultural water management using a robotic framework that integrates deep learning and fuzzy logic for real-time crop classification and decision-making. It employs a combination of VGG-19 and a fusion model RTCropNet (Real-time crop network), leveraging the strengths of each architecture: VGG-19 for robust feature extraction and the RTCropNet fusion for enhanced spatial localization and fine-grained crop classification. Pre-processing is performed through advanced fuzzy logic techniques to improve image quality, enhancing classification accuracy across diverse crop types. Evaluation metrics indicate that the RTCropNet model achieves a training accuracy of 80.15% and a validation accuracy of 81.77%, with precision, recall, and F1 scores of 0.83, 0.82, and 0.82, respectively, outperforming traditional methods on complex agricultural imagery. Comparative analysis shows the model's superiority over EfficientNet-B3, DenseNet-121, and MobileNetV2, particularly in handling high-resolution spatial details, while maintaining efficiency in real-time conditions. This integration of deep learning with fuzzy logic and sensor data represents a novel approach in precision irrigation, offering a dynamic, data-driven response system that adjusts irrigation based on real-time environmental conditions, distinguishing it from conventional SOTA approaches.

articleTitle: Classification models for improved prediction of autism spectrum disorder: behavioural and facial feature analysis using machine learning approach
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental condition that significantly affects social relationships, interaction, behavior, learning capabilities, and knowledge acquisition. Despite its global prevalence and progressive nature, timely diagnosis remains challenging. This work aims to develop a machine learning classifier model to accurately predict the likelihood of ASD by utilizing dataset comprising both behavioral and facial image features from children. ASD symptoms typically appear and develop more between ages 3 and 11, with early signs often misinterpreted as other conditions, such as intellectual disability, which delays accurate diagnosis. Diagnosing ASD involves evaluating developmental history and observing behaviors, and processes that require considerable expertise and time. Recently, machine learning and deep learning have shown promise in ASD research, particularly in enhancing diagnostic accuracy through data analysis. The models employed in this study include Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbours, Support Vector Machine, Extra Tree, Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network. Using the image-based data, the SVM model achieves 70% accuracy in image classification, while the ET and LR models yield 100% accuracy using the AQ-10 screening dataset, outperforming other models analyzed. This research demonstrates the potential of machine learning models in improving the accuracy of ASD diagnosis by integrating behavioral and facial image data. The findings suggest that employing diverse dataset and advanced algorithms can significantly enhance the diagnostic process.

articleTitle: Forecasting traits: human personality prediction with machine learning methodology - a comparative study
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Data science and AI are transforming the planet through technological change. We can look at many applications of machine learning in our daily lives, but one of the most widely used applications of machine learning is to categorize individuals based on their personality traits. Everyone on this planet is unique and carries a personality—a special kind of character. The availability of high-quality data has paved the way for more effective marketing campaigns targeted at specific demographic groups for predictive analytics and behavioural psychology. Such personality-based communication is more effective in creating more acceptable and appealing products and services. This research work proposes a framework for predicting personality using big five personality traits. Throughout the globe, people are exposed to competitive exams that focus mainly on their personality evaluation. The main motivation behind these assessments is to test the personality and skill sets of people. From personality classification, one can also determine the type of personality and improve the personality based on the results. In this context, we have utilized machine learning models such as Random Forest Classifier, Decision Tree Classifier, Ada-Boost Classifier and hybrid XGB - eXtreme Gradient Boosting Classifier for forecasting traits – personality prediction. The investigations were validated with four performance metrics; accuracy, precision, recall and f1 score. Throughout the experimentations, the hybrid XGB Classifier outperformed all the other algorithms with an accuracy of 95.66%. The precision, recall and f1-success of the hybrid XGB Classifier were evaluated to be 96% respectively.

articleTitle: Integration of SSID and blockchain technology for advanced knowledge management system
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The integration of a blockchain-oriented knowledge management system with Self-Sovereign Identity (SSID) marks a pivotal shift from traditional centralized methods to a decentralized paradigm. The Self-Sovereign Identity(SSID) refers to a digital identity system that makes users independent and allows users to control their own data without depending on central authority.This research paper has underscored the transformative potential of this innovative approach, presenting a robust solution with enhanced security features. By leveraging blockchain technology, the knowledge management system achieves unprecedented levels of transparency, immutability, and tamper resistance. The decentralized nature ensures that data is distributed across a network, mitigating the vulnerabilities associated with a single- point-of-failure inherent in centralized systems. This not only safeguards sensitive information but also promotes trust among users, fostering a more resilient and secure ecosystem. The incorporation of Self-Sovereign Identity adds an extra layer of privacy and user control. Users maintain ownership and control over their identity information, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and identity theft. This paradigm shift aligns with the principles of user empowerment, providing individuals with greater autonomy in managing their digital identities. The synergistic interplay between blockchain and SSID not only enhances security but also paves the way for a more transparent, efficient, and user-centric knowledge management ecosystem.

articleTitle: Utilizing windows event logs for malware detection using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: As the occurrence of cyber threats rise continuously, Windows Operating System serve as both vulnerable sites and strongholds in today’s digital domain. This research delivers into an exhaustive inquiry on cyber-attack pattern focuses on filtering Windows environments coupled with a thorough investigation of state-of-the-art detection remedies. The research diligently scrutinizes widespread malware attack practices like advance malware techniques or customized hacks while breaking down their tactics and approaches and length. Windows logs are a crucial component of the Windows Operating System, capturing events and activities to provide administrators with valuable insights into system health and performance. Administrators often leverage Windows logs for troubleshooting, monitoring and security analysis, utilizing the rich data stored within them to ensure the stability and security of their Windows-based systems. Our model aims to detect malware that bypasses firewalls and traditional antimalware by analysing system event logs for behaviour anomalies, focusing on unauthorized access patterns rather than relying on IoCs alone. In this paper we used windows logs and convert the logs captured into a useful dataset to detect the malicious activity by the malwares and finding the best solution for prevent the attacks.

articleTitle: Intelligent irrigation system with multiple nodes and smart sensors using IoT for agricultural field
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Agriculture is the primary line of occupation for most of the Indian peoples. In India about 58% of people are working on agricultural as it is their main source of income. But the sane place farmers are facing the issues like irrigation, lack of modernization and surface water overexploitation. The proposed automated irrigation system integrates multiple nodes equipped with NPK sensors, Node MCU, and PIC microcontrollers to monitor soil moisture and nutrition levels in real-time. Utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technology, the system enables remote monitoring and control using Thingspeak. The NPK sensors provide accurate data on soil nutrient content, allowing for precise and targeted fertilization. To prevent well motor pump dry-run and enhance system efficiency, the current sensor attached to power cable of well motor pump. The system consists of a network of nodes purposefully placed across the agricultural field, each equipped with smart sensors capable of monitoring crucial environmental vales like soil moisture level, atmospheric temperature value, and humidity level. Furthermore, the system offers a user-friendly interface accessible through web or mobile applications, allowing farmers to monitor and control the irrigation process remotely. The IoT based intelligent irrigation system is not only enhancing water efficiency but also contributes to sustainable agriculture practices. By reducing water consumption and minimizing environmental impact, the proposed system aims to improve overall crop yield and foster a more resilient and adaptive approach to modern farming. As technology continues to evolve, integrating intelligent solutions in agriculture becomes crucial for ensuring food security and sustainability in the face of changing global conditions.

articleTitle: A synchronized approach to denoising medical images through deep learning
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Medical imaging plays a crucial role in modern healthcare, aiding in the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases. However, noise during acquisition frequently taints medical images, lowering their quality and making diagnosis more difficult. Deep learning methods have demonstrated encouraging outcomes in medical image denoising recently, providing a viable remedy for this problem. This study compares two well-known deep learning architectures for denoising medical images: Residual Neural Network (ResNet) and Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN). The purpose of the study is to assess these architectures' performance in terms of key image feature preservation and noise reduction efficacy. Firstly, a thorough introduction to deep learning techniques and medical image denoising is given, emphasizing how crucial it is to accurately reduce noise while maintaining diagnostic information. Then the detailed descriptions of these architectures are explained highlighting their special qualities and applicability to denoising applications. Training and testing the DCNN and ResNet models on a dataset of different medical images tainted by different kinds and intensities of noise constitutes the experimental setup. Each model's denoising performance is statistically assessed using performance metrics such as Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and visual quality assessment. The simulation results show how well DCNN and ResNet architectures perform in lowering noise in medical images. Comparative analysis, however, reveals variations in their computational effectiveness and denoising capacities. Furthermore, qualitative evaluations show that these models can eliminate noise artifacts while maintaining significant anatomical details and textures. Overall, this comparison study highlights the benefits and drawbacks of the ResNet and DCNN designs and offers insightful information about the use of deep learning approaches for denoising medical images. The results support further efforts to raise the standard and dependability of medical imaging for better patient care and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Automated detection and classification of rice leaf diseases using YOLOv8: a deep learning approach for enhanced crop monitoring
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Rice is a staple food crop, and its cultivation is crucial for ensuring global food security. However, rice plant diseases pose a significant threat to crop yields, emphasizing the need for effective disease detection and management strategies. With the rapid advancements in machine learning and computer vision techniques, there has been a growing interest in leveraging these technologies for automated disease detection in agriculture. Common diseases affecting rice plants, such as blast, brown spot, and bacterial blight, can cause substantial yield losses if left undetected and untreated. Early and accurate detection of these diseases is essential for implementing timely and targeted control measures, ultimately minimizing crop damage and maximizing yields. In this research, we propose the use of deep learning techniques, specifically the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm, for the automated detection and classification of rice leaf diseases. The methodology involves training the YOLOv8 model on a carefully curated dataset comprising 2,304 annotated images of rice leaves, capturing diverse disease manifestations as well as healthy samples. The dataset was labeled, ensuring accurate ground truth for model training and evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning model achieved an impressive accuracy of 68.2% in correctly classifying healthy rice leaf samples. This promising outcome highlights the potential of the YOLOv8 algorithm for practical applications in rice leaf disease detection and monitoring.

articleTitle: Advanced AI solution to detect Parkinson's disease through voice data analysis
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: The affliction referred to as Parkinson's disease (PD) results in a continuous decline in neurological performance, evident through assorted motor and non-motor symptoms that are being more widely discovered internationally. The prompt and precise identification of PD is essential for facilitating timely interventions and enhancing patient well-being. This scholarly article delves into a multitude of innovative techniques and strategies for the early identification of Parkinson's disease, spotlighting the utilization of deep learning models harnessed from the UCI Parkinson's disease remote monitoring dataset. Evaluating the severity of Parkinson's disease relies heavily on the UPDRS as a significant resource. In facing the challenges of multicollinearity within the dataset and optimizing the dimensionality of the spatial data, methodologies like Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and its extensions, including kernelPCA, incremental PCA, and sparse PCA, alongside Independent Component Analysis (ICA), are carried out. The results of these dimensionality reductions were subsequently fed into Deep Neural Network (DNN) models, which were configured with diverse parameters to assess their efficacy in predicting mobility and Total-UPDRS scores during the manifestation of PD. The model's performance is scrutinized through evaluations, and the findings are juxtaposed with those from earlier models utilizing the same dataset. To determine the model's precision, we scrutinize performance measures including mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) to gain insights into the dependability of the forecasts. We also tested several different model designs with different hyperparameters on the same dataset. Among all the variants of the DNN model, we obtained the best results using DNN variant 2 of the 8-component sparse PCA. The MAE, MSE and values for the motor UPDRS are 0.0622, 0.0126, respectively. For the total UPDRS, we obtained the values of 0.0935 and 0.0185, respectively.

articleTitle: Proactive detection of Mirai botnet threats: leveraging XGBoost for enhanced cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Detecting the Mirai botnet is still a key challenge in cybersecurity because of the continuous growth of hostile tactics. Existing detection systems frequently rely on antiquated methodologies, resulting in low accuracy and efficiency. The study indicates a novel approach for detecting Mirai botnet activity that uses XGBoost, an advanced ensemble learning algorithm. The proposed system outperforms standard approaches in terms of performance measures by incorporating thorough data preparation, feature extraction, and selection methodologies, as well as efficient XGBoost model training. The results show a considerable improvement in accuracy (0.90), precision (0.89), recall (0.91), and F1 score (0.90), as well as a decrease in false positives (20) and false negatives (15). Furthermore, improved computational efficiency leads to shorter training and prediction timeframes, less memory utilization, and more responsive detection capabilities. Overall, the proposed system provides a strong framework for proactive detection and mitigation of Mirai botnet threats, which improves network security in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Computer-aided diagnosis of psoriasis classification using deep learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Psoriasis is a long-term autoimmune skin disorder that impacts millions of individuals globally. Early diagnosis of psoriasis enables timely intervention, helping to prevent the progression of the condition and manage symptoms more efficiently. In this research, proposed an algorithm for Psoriasis Detection System using CNN-VGG16 algorithm, AlexNet and SqueezeNet to automate the identification of different psoriatic lesions in skin images. The CNN architecture is built to automatically extract distinguishing features from input images, allowing the system to differentiate between normal and psoriatic skin patterns. The model undergoes rigorous training and validation processes to optimize its performance. The Proposed AlexNet and SqueezNet both demonstrated good results with accuracies of 94.4% and 96.3%, respectively, but the CNN-VGG16 surpassed all other models with an accuracy of 97.22%. The outcomes of this research contribute to the advancement of automated psoriasis detection systems, offering a reliable and efficient tool for dermatologists and healthcare professionals.

articleTitle: AI based forest fire detection using deep learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Forest fires pose serious risks to ecological components, infrastructure, and human life. It is projected that half of the forest ecosystems would have been completely destroyed by wildfires by 2030. Reducing the damage caused by forest fires can only be accomplished by using fire detection devices. As a result, study centers and universities all around the world are paying close attention to forest-fire detection techniques. There are already several different commercial automated fire sensor systems available, but they are all difficult to use in wide open regions like woodlands because of their poor reaction times, high maintenance needs, and other problems. Image processing has been used in this study due to the quick development of digital camera technology, the camera's excellent coverage of wide areas, the faster response time of image processing methods compared to established sensor systems, and the general lower cost of image processing systems compared to sensor systems. False alarm rates may be substantial since certain objects have characteristics with forest fires, which make reliable forest fire detection systems challenging. This study presents a revolutionary four-stage video-based image processing approach for forest fire detection. First, a background-subtraction approach is applied to identify moving zones. Second, potential fire zones are located using RGB colour space. Thirdly, features extraction is used to differentiate between actual fire and fire-like objects since candidate zones may contain moving fire-like objects. Finally, the convolutional neural network method is used to classify the region of interest as either a genuine fire or not. The results of the last experiment show that the recommended strategy finds forest fires with success.

articleTitle: Fashion fusion: generating trendy attire with Indian ethnic art using text-to-image generative model
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Designing fashion apparel with local trends and styles, holds significant potential for retailers and consumers. Fashion designers invest considerable time and effort in creating designs based on print/pattern and attribute selection. To address the challenges posed by manual efforts and achieve automation, this article introduces a novel framework for designers, incorporating specific styles (prints/patterns) and attribute information via generative models. The proposed method fine- tunes the Stable Diffusion XL, a text-to-image (T2I) generative model, using a dataset of images featuring Kolam or Gond tribal arts from South and Central India, respectively. These images help to infuse region-specific print/pattern styles into T-shirts/Kurtas. Additionally, input attributes such as neck type and, sleeve type are integrated with text prompts during inference to produce the final fashion attire. A comprehensive evaluation was carried out and compared with state-of-the-art T2I models. The results indicate 75.78% accuracy in attribute and 76% in styles.

articleTitle: Prediction and identification of multiple sclerosis patients from gait features using machine learning algorithms and ensemble methods in embedded sensors environment
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic autoimmune disease prevalent among mid-aged to younger adults. The objectives of implementing advanced computational techniques in gait feature analysis are to refine the analytical process, improve the accuracy of gait assessment and understanding human locomotion patterns to predict and identify the multiple sclerosis patient using logistic regression, Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbours classifiers. We aim to automate the analysis of gait feature data collected from various sensors to expedite the prediction and identification of multiple sclerosis. This automation facilitates the early detection of subtle deviations in gait dynamics, which could signify neurological impairments. Logistic regression, Support Vector Machine and KNN models are capable of processing intricate gait data to discern meaningful patterns and characteristics indicative of multiple sclerosis conditions with minimum number of gait features. This paper introduces new gait features to improve the model’s performance and differentiate the multiple sclerosis from healthy control group. KNN demonstrates superior accuracy (96.55%) compared to Support Vector Machine (90.05%) and logistic regression (86.35%). KNN with bagging achieved the highest prediction accuracy (94.4%), while logistic regression with bagging had the lowest (83.3%). This paper proposes an ensemble learning method that uses weight averaging to get combine the predictions of above models with ensemble accuracy of 90.12%. A new index called match index is created for the identification of multiple sclerosis.

articleTitle: Explainable AI and deep learning for brain tumour classification using grad-CAM visualization
publicationTitle: 2nd International Conference on Computer Vision and Internet of Things (ICCVIoT 2024)
abstract: Brain tumours rank as the fifth most common cancer type, affecting approximately 90,000 people annually and pose high risks due to their potential for life-threatening neurological impacts. Traditional diagnostic methods often lack visualization clarity, impeding accurate interpretation and delaying critical treatment decisions. To address these challenges, this study introduces a robust deep learning framework that combines ResNet101, InceptionV3, DenseNet201 and VGG16 architectures to classify brain tumours into four categories: pituitary, meningioma, glioma and no tumour. The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 7,022 MRI images and was finely tuned to maximize classification accuracy. Additionally, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to generate interpretable heatmaps, highlighting key regions in MRI scans that influence classification. This enhanced interpretability facilitates clinical trust and understanding by allowing the model's focus areas to align with clinically relevant regions. The combined model achieved a highly competitive performance, with 99.2% accuracy, 98.8% precision, 98.7% recall and an F1-score of 99.1%, along with an AUC of 1.00 across all classes, reflecting robust diagnostic potential. Grad-CAM was specifically applied to tumour classes, revealing critical areas in MRI scans and supporting improved interpretability. This framework marks a substantial advancement in brain tumour classification, streamlining the diagnostic process, minimizing reliance on manual interpretation and fostering more efficient, accurate and sustainable healthcare solutions.
